solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What artist does is attractive

definitions.meaning: an artist sketches pictures with a pencil
a show that pulls in crowds is said to bring them in, entice them

explanation.surface: A remark that an artist at work has a certain appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same verb: an artist sketches, and something appealing pulls people towards it.

clue.text: Bottle after bottle?

parts.note: bottle is slang for nerve, and the bravery meant here comes after a bottle or two of drink

explanation.surface: A drinker working through one bottle after another.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang bottle means courage; the answer is the boldness found after drinking from a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom names the false bravery that alcohol gives a nervous person.

clue.text: Lakeland setting for youth leader

indicators.note: the word Lakeland is the setting in which the letters sit

explanation.surface: The Lake District as a backdrop for a leader of young people.
explanation.walkthrough: Lakeland is the Lake District of north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The adult leader of a Cub Scout pack takes this title from the wolf in The Jungle Book.

clue.text: Small furry animal, extremely 7, spruced up

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a marten is a weasel-like mammal with fine fur

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the end letters are kept

parts.note: the answer to clue 7, meaning wasted

explanation.surface: A tiny, very skinny furry creature has been tidied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the end letters ED of the answer to 7-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Made neater and smarter in appearance, a synonym phrase for tidied.

clue.text: Obliged to survey Englishmen on vacation

parts.note: to survey a scene is to look upon it, an old word for which is behold

indicators.note: a word on vacation has been emptied, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone feels duty-bound to inspect English people who are away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties Englishmen, leaving EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being indebted or under an obligation to someone is the standard sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Vehicle that is top of range is less available

parts.note: a bus is a road vehicle
ie is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

indicators.note: in a down answer, the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A top-of-the-range vehicle is harder to get hold of.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone more occupied has less free time, so is harder to see or book.

clue.text: Rick and Henry always succeeded on course

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
ay is a poetic word for always, also spelt aye
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
a tack is a sailing course set against the wind

explanation.surface: Two men, Rick and Henry, who were always a success at the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rick' looks like a man's name, but here it is a stack of hay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rick is a large built pile of hay or straw in a field.

clue.text: Soft fabric supplier from America completely revolutionised

indicators.note: turned round in a revolution, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: all means wholly or completely

explanation.surface: A soft cloth maker from America has utterly transformed its business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionised' reverses AMALL.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American animal yields wool used for soft cloth, so it supplies fabric.

clue.text: Eastern spies with yoked clothing wasted

indicators.note: the outer word clothes the inner one by surrounding it

parts.note: animals yoked together are paired, or mated
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: Eastern agents in harness, their clothing worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like garments in the surface, but it signals one piece wrapped round another.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thin and gaunt from illness or hunger is described as wasted away.

clue.text: Queen's night attire simply the best?

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, so the queen's things are a cat's
pyjamas are what one wears to bed

explanation.surface: A pun on what a queen might wear to bed, posed as the very best of things.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests royalty, but a queen is also a female cat. The question mark flags that the phrase is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: This dated slang idiom describes something excellent or first-rate, like the bee's knees.

clue.text: Caterer found bananas for lengthy sporting event

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: A caterer supplied fruit for a long race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' rearranges CATERER FOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous three-week cycle race around France is a long sporting event.

clue.text: Genuine theft, real criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone insists a theft was truly real and criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges the letters of THEFT and REAL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings that are sincere and deeply meant are described with this adjective, a synonym of sincere.

clue.text: Contrary old soldier, mother's mate from abroad

indicators.note: contrary means going the opposite way, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: An awkward veteran is described as the friend of somebody's mum from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary' turns OGIMA round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a friend is borrowed into English, so it means a pal from a foreign land.

clue.text: Present playing cards for the individual

parts.note: something playing, as a show or film, is on
the cards dealt to one player form a hand

explanation.surface: A card game in progress, with each player's cards given out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being available and nearby, ready when needed, is what this phrase means, like the adjective present.

clue.text: Shock solution's risky, Superman from time to time admitted

indicators.note: the letters are let in to the other word

parts.note: hairy is informal for dangerous or risky

indicators.note: only now and then are letters taken, so alternate ones

explanation.surface: A risky shocking concoction, with Superman letting it in now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' is a thick head of hair, not a jolt; 'from time to time' picks alternate letters and 'admitted' lets them in.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair is held in place with a fixing spray, a liquid solution.

clue.text: Be marked, cut by one German with sword

indicators.note: the word for being marked is sliced open with other letters put in

parts.note: to scar is to be left with a mark, as skin is
I is the Roman numeral for one
mit is German for with

explanation.surface: A warning that one might be scarred, slashed by a German swordsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' supplies a German word rather than an abbreviation; 'cut by' says the marking word is split open to take the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved, single-edged blade of Middle Eastern origin is a kind of sword.

clue.text: Mum going round university in Paris arranged a place for Joey

indicators.note: going round suggests the letters circling and churning into a fresh order
the letters are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: A mother in Paris arranging university for a child named Joey.
explanation.walkthrough: A joey is a baby kangaroo, so a place for one is its mother's pouch; 'going round' and 'arranged' both stir the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The pouch in which a marsupial carries its young is a home for a baby kangaroo.

clue.text: Company porters attending church merge in

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, and beers are ales
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A firm's porters join a church and blend in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porters' looks like luggage carriers, but porter is a dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To come together and form one whole is to unite or fuse, a synonym of merge.

clue.text: Artillery arriving by parachute, presumably causing a bit of a splash?

definitions.text: presumably causing a bit of a splash?

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British Army regiment
something arriving has come in
a parachute landing of troops or supplies is a drop

explanation.surface: Guns coming in by parachute would make quite an entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a single falling drop of water makes a small splash.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop of precipitation falling from a cloud makes a tiny splash where it lands.

clue.text: Nurse, close to despair in scoundrel's grip, fled unclothed

indicators.note: the letter sits within the scoundrel's grasp
the scoundrel holds the letter in its grip, surrounding it

parts.note: a cad is an ungentlemanly rogue

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter
a word unclothed has its outer letters stripped away

explanation.surface: A nurse in despair, held by a villain, ran off without her clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' takes R from despair, held in CAD; 'unclothed' strips fled to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a baby can mean to hold it gently in one's arms, a synonym of this verb.

clue.text: The author's facade's put on

parts.note: the setter speaking is the author, and the author is becomes I'm
a pose is a pretence or false front

explanation.surface: A writer admits their outward show is just an act.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something on someone, a burden or tax, is to force it upon them.

clue.text: Pants son's wearing split more than once

indicators.note: the gaps put on the letter like clothing, so it goes inside them

parts.note: several splits are gaps
S is the abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A boy's trousers have torn in several places while he wears them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' reads as trousers, but it is the verb for breathing hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pants is breathing in short, quick breaths, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Loner's curious since travelling north

indicators.note: in a down answer, travelling north means reading upwards

parts.note: odd means strange or curious
as can mean since, as in as it rained

explanation.surface: A solitary person is odd because they are heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling north' reverses ODDAS; the answer is British slang for a pitiable loner.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a sad, socially inept person, often one who keeps to themselves.

clue.text: Person applying pressure on branch to supply cheese

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: a limb is a large branch of a tree
one who urges or presses another is an urger

explanation.surface: Someone pushing on a tree branch to supply some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong-smelling soft cheese from the Limburg region of Belgium and the Netherlands.

clue.text: Harsh year, marked by pollution

parts.note: grim means harsh or severe

explanation.surface: A harsh year that was spoiled by pollution.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covered in dirt or soot, as from smog, is dirty-looking.

clue.text: Penchant, eg. for arresting police inspectors

indicators.note: the outer word arrests, or holds, the police officers inside it

parts.note: the word for is an example of a preposition
DIs are detective inspectors

explanation.surface: A liking for detaining police officers, given as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eg. for' looks like part of the definition, but 'for' is an example of a part of speech; 'arresting' places DIS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural tendency or inclination towards something, much like a liking or leaning.

clue.text: Mineral is extracted from fluid epoxy resin

indicators.note: the two letters of is are drawn out of the mixed letters
fluid means changeable, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mineral being separated out of runny glue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluid' mixes EPOXY RESIN; 'extracted from' removes I and S, leaving the answer's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of silicate minerals common in igneous rocks goes by this name.

clue.text: Springtime sound from insect, perhaps

parts.note: May is a spring month

indicators.note: the letters are what the insect's name sounds like when spoken

parts.note: a bee is a stinging insect

explanation.surface: The buzz of an insect heard in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound from' signals that BEE is heard as BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words express possibility or uncertainty, synonyms for possibly.
